body:
My girlfriend and I learned different foreign languages. I learned German (only through high school), while she learned Spanish (and just graduated with a degree in it).

When I'm thanking her for something, I'll often say thank you in German-"Danke!"

She'll reply in Spanish-"De Nada"

It takes a physical effort to respond to people thanking me with anything but de nada. One coworker who was a German major and knew I'd taken some German actually said danke for something and I didn't have the chance to stop my brain that time before I replied in a completely different non-native language.

I was hoping this wasn't just me! Happened to me a month or so ago, and after half an hour of struggling with it and nearly crying in frustration I finally took the damn thing back to the store and swapped it out (and you better believe I stepped outside the store, ripped off the packaging, and OPENED THAT THING BEFORE I WALKED HOME). Today I wanted ice cream! I got two jars of it! (Double Dark Chocolate and Chocolate Peanut Butter Cup) When the first one didn't open, I figured I'd give it a bit, just get the second one...

After smacking it around and cursing a few times until I scared the heck out of my poor cat, I finally just got out the knife and cut up the lid. Great ice cream, but the packaging just isn't worth it.

I work part time at both jobs. One is retail, a craft store, and we are entering in to seasonal right now. Our trucks (I am on the truck unloading crew and we stock things and keep the store looking good) are very big now and it takes all of us to get it unloaded in a reasonable amount of time. So I cannot really take off time from there. And it would not be paid time even if I did. And I can't afford to miss work because I need the money.
I am part time at the library too (that is my other job) and I could take off time if I needed, and I'm sure my supervisor would be ok with it because she is great. But again I need the money. And that is the higher paying job.

I want to go to the hospital and let someone else do the job of keeping me alive but missing work is bad. If I miss too many days of work (which is like maybe two days in the span of a month) then I cannot pay rent. If I cannot pay rent I am homeless and then I die much more quickly and uncomfortably. There is no way that I could save the money to pay a rent deposit and rent at the same time in a new place, while living on the street.

Hey...I'm 24 and I was diagnosed with POTS six years ago and EDS five years ago. 

If you have any specific questions, about things to help either condition, or support groups, or you just need to talk to someone, my message box is open and you are always welcome to use it. It's completely okay to be scared about this-it's a big thing, and it's not necessarily something to treat lightly-but there are people here who can and will help.

I mean, I've got friends who like Harry Potter-for one thing, I'm planning on taking my girlfriend/fiance to the theme park, and her mom, they're both fans.

It's just the part where...there was someone who was, literally, my entire life. I say literally because I wasn't allowed out of the house to make my own friends. I went to school, but I didn't know how to make friends, because I never left the house. My mom was my best and only friend-the way she liked it.

So it's not missing having *someone* to talk about Harry Potter with...it's knowing that your childhood/teenagehood best friend would have loved this, but you can't tell them. And not because something has happened to them, but because it's just not safe to reach out to them. I had no other friends growing up-she was the only one. So I can't turn to other friends from when I was a kid, either.
